key_insight: Spin-current transmission through epitaxial α-Fe2O3 is strongly temperature- and thickness-dependent, with a characteristic transition temperature linked to the magnetic reorientation of the hematite layer.
engineering_relevance: This suggests antiferromagnetic oxide thickness and operating temperature can be used to tune spintronic device performance and signal transfer efficiency.
method: Epitaxial α-Fe2O3 thin films were sandwiched between Permalloy and Pt.
Spin pumping was used to generate spin current and inverse spin Hall effect to detect the resulting dc voltage.
Samples with α-Fe2O3 thicknesses of 0, 30, 40, and 100 nm were measured from 1.6 to 300 K.
evidence_signal: A finite symmetric dc voltage was observed across Pt for all studied films, and the temperature coefficient Ks showed two linear regimes separated by a thickness-dependent T* that correlates with the Morin transition.
watch_item: The spin-transport response appears highly sensitive to magnetic phase changes and structural defects, so device behavior may vary substantially with film quality and thermal operating point.
paper_title: Temperature and Thickness Dependent Spin Current Transmission through Epitaxial Antiferromagnetic α-Fe2O3
